clue.text: Businessman's accessory suitable to go in cut

indicators.note: the word for suitable is told to go inside the word for cut, a container signal

parts.note: to lop is to cut off, as with branches
apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: A tip for executives: some accessory fits neatly into a trim.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable computer is a standard piece of kit carried by people in business.

clue.text: A ceremony broadcast properly

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the airwaves, so the ceremony word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony or ritual

explanation.surface: A ceremony gets aired on television without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns RITE into the word that sounds the same, RIGHT, after the A that the clue gives as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Done correctly or in the right way: an old-fashioned adverb meaning rightly.

clue.text: A little drunk, gives silent signal for game

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk
someone who winks gives a wordless signal with one eye

explanation.surface: A tipsy guest keeps winking across the table, signalling it is time to play.
explanation.walkthrough: TIDDLY is everyday British slang for slightly tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's pastime in which small counters are flicked into a cup with a larger disc.

clue.text: Paris not bad setting for upper-class follower of French recluse

indicators.note: the rearranged letters form a setting, like a jewel's mount, around the upper-class letter
bad means the letters of Paris and not are spoilt and put in a new order

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for upper-class, as in U and non-U usage

explanation.surface: Paris is a pleasant enough backdrop for some aristocratic admirer of a reclusive French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not bad' reads as 'quite good', but 'not' is fodder and 'bad' alone is the anagram signal, giving PROSTIAN; 'setting for' then mounts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust, who wrote in a cork-lined room and shunned society, gives an adjective for his admirers and imitators.

clue.text: Wood, if fractionally incomplete, split

indicators.note: only an incomplete stretch of these words is used, the letters running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A piece of timber, if it is broken off a little short, has split.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Wood' through 'if' into the start of 'fractionally'; 'incomplete' signals that only part of the words is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, to bend and spread light or other waves as they pass an edge or slit, breaking them up.

clue.text: Magistrate maintains exclusion order for supposed pet poisoner

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the magistrate's title holds the order inside it

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
a ban is an order shutting someone or something out

explanation.surface: A judge upholds a banning order against a plant suspected of poisoning animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The doge was the elected chief magistrate of old Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant whose name records the old belief that it was toxic to hounds and other household animals.

clue.text: Cast wild spell

explanation.surface: A witch throws an untamed incantation.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw something hard is one sense; a short period of carefree, often romantic indulgence is the other.

clue.text: Half-built school theatre

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Half-built school theatre (3)' with answer REP, matching the scan: 'theatre' gives REP (repertory), but no reading of 'Half-built school' giving REP could be found or confirmed by search.

clue.text: Duke had poor nun executed once

parts.note: a member of the Poor Clares, the Franciscan order of nuns, is a Clare

indicators.note: executed means beheaded here, so the word once loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Some nobleman had a destitute nun put to death long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' means beheaded: ONCE loses its head to give NCE. The surface fits: a Duke of Clarence was himself executed in 1478, supposedly drowned in a butt of malmsey wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarence is a royal dukedom, held most famously by Edward IV's brother George.

clue.text: With call of nature, boy on time — good!

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the boy comes after the time

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, time served
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A child on a timed walk dashes off to relieve himself, and all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call of nature' usually means a trip to the lavatory; here it is the sound of the wild. BIRD, prison time, is from rhyming slang 'bird-lime'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song of a bird is literally a call heard in nature.

clue.text: Not crossing boundary with Shakespeare production?

explanation.surface: An actor stays within the lines while a Shakespeare play goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball still within the field of play has not crossed the boundary; a character appearing in a staged drama is, whimsically, inside a play.

clue.text: Philosopher's stories hard to penetrate

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the hard letter is to penetrate, that is go into, the word for stories

parts.note: tales are stories
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A thinker's yarns prove tough to get into.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Thales of Miletus was an early Greek thinker, often named as the first in the Western tradition.

clue.text: Merchant vessels given sign, about to turn south

indicators.note: about means around, so the sign's letters go around the others

parts.note: Aries, the Ram, is a sign of the zodiac
a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: Trading ships, given a signal, are about to swing round to the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning a turn in a game, as in 'your go'; 'about' wraps the sign around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Large merchant ships of old, named after the Adriatic port of Ragusa.

clue.text: One's sally is reprinted when there's little else to report

definitions.text: when there's little else to report

indicators.note: something reprinted is set again in type, so these letters are reset in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, its letters O, N, E and S

explanation.surface: Someone's witty remark is run again in the paper because there is nothing new to print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reprinted' tells you to rearrange ONES, SALLY and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: The summer lull in British journalism when trivial stories fill the papers because politics is quiet.

clue.text: Pad, and why one can't write on it?

definitions.text: why one can't write on it?

explanation.surface: A notepad, and the reason someone cannot get words down on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'on it' makes the second definition point back at the pad: the paper is there, the words are not.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper is a block for writers to use; a creative barrier that stops an author producing anything is the other sense.

clue.text: Frustrate, then encourage to have a snack

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to frustrate or thwart it
to egg someone on is to encourage them

explanation.surface: A party thwarts a plan, then urges someone to grab a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A SCOTCH EGG is a British picnic snack: a hard-boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold savoury item eaten as a light bite or picnic food.

clue.text: Vetoing a move to accept local ideas

indicators.note: move is an instruction to shift the letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: Refusing a proposal so as to take on the views of the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' looks like a noun, a proposal being vetoed, but it is the instruction to rearrange VETOING A.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an outsider adopting the customs and outlook of the people they live among.

clue.text: After pronounced sorrow, praise for early-closing plant

indicators.note: the praise word comes after the sorrow word in the answer
pronounced means spoken, so the sorrow word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: mourning is grief or sorrow
glory is praise, as in glory to God

explanation.surface: After voicing grief, someone praises a plant that shuts at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' turns MOURNING into its soundalike MORNING. 'early-closing' plays on British shop half-days: the flowers shut by afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant whose trumpet flowers open at dawn and fade later the same day.

clue.text: Have a bad spell, playing snooker?

explanation.surface: Someone at the snooker table suffers a slump in form.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for deteriorating badly is one sense; in snooker, aiming a ball at a pocket is the whimsical second.

clue.text: Burst of extravagance, wasting pounds for plant

indicators.note: wasting means losing or using up, so the pound letter is dropped from the spree word

parts.note: a splurge is a sudden bout of lavish spending
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A spending spree that squanders money on a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia is a large genus of plants with milky sap.

clue.text: Tongue got right in sketch by nursing-home

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the two parts side by side

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a place of convalescent care

indicators.note: the right letter goes in the sketch word

parts.note: a skit is a short comic sketch

explanation.surface: A language gets things right in a comedy sketch staged beside a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' is a language here, not part of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient classical language of India.

clue.text: Was in charge of Church Farm

parts.note: someone who ran a business was in charge of it

explanation.surface: Someone managed a farm belonging to the parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cattle or livestock estate, especially in North America.

clue.text: Extremely affordable jumble firm holds

indicators.note: the firm's abbreviation holds the jumble word inside it

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a heap is an untidy pile, a jumble

explanation.surface: A company keeps a very cheap pile of jumble-sale goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumble' looks like the usual signal to rearrange, but it is a noun meaning a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A slangy word for something very cheap or low cost.

clue.text: Tribe's exhausting trouble in Jerusalem

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the trouble goes in the word for Jerusalem

parts.note: Sion or Zion is a name for Jerusalem
ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, is an illness marked by exhaustion

explanation.surface: A tribe suffers draining hardship in the holy city.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is the British name for chronic fatigue syndrome. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the twelve tribes of Israel, descended from a son of Jacob.

clue.text: Be likely not to start or finish

indicators.note: not to start means the word's opening letter is left off

parts.note: to tend to do something is to be likely to do it

explanation.surface: It is probably best neither to begin nor to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to start' removes the first letter from TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclusion or close, a synonym for the final point.

clue.text: Start to listen to Sea Drift in sheer delight

indicators.note: the letters go in the word for sheer

parts.note: sheer means pure, as in pure nonsense

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the word listen
drift means the letters of Sea wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Begin hearing Delius's Sea Drift and be thoroughly enchanted.
explanation.walkthrough: Sea Drift is a choral work by Delius, so 'Drift' looks like part of a title; it is the anagram signal, making EAS, and 'Start to' takes the first letter of 'listen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enjoyment or happiness, a synonym for great satisfaction.

clue.text: Marksman hates odd mistakes

indicators.note: mistakes, read as a verb, means gets the letters wrong, putting them out of order

explanation.surface: A sniper detests the occasional error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakes' reads as a noun but is the verb that rearranges HATES ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shoots with deadly accuracy.

clue.text: Teams working round English river

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the teams word goes round the English letter

parts.note: gangs are teams of labourers at work

explanation.surface: Work crews toil around an English waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred watercourse of northern India.
